title: The four editors and how Jazzmen was put together
summary: Who edited Jazzmen, the contract, why only Ramsey's name went on the cover, and who gathered photographs.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Was there anything else in Jasmine besides Bessie Smith and Jelly Roll that was planned but didn't...
I can't think of anything now.

I wanted to ask you how... I don't know whether... How did Ramsey and Smith... It says edited by Frederick Ramsey Jr. and Charles Edward Smith. Did they go through the whole book and decide which was going in and which was going left out?

No, that was all decided before. Actually, another funny thing was I don't even have my contract to prove it anymore. There were four editors, supposedly. Steve Smith and I were also listed as editors in the original contract and the idea was that we got a bigger... a bigger share of the advance or something by being an editor that way. We got more money to work with... I guess some of the others didn't even get $30 maybe. I don't know what the advance was. As I said, I don't even remember any details of the finances of it. But there were four editors but there couldn't be four editors on the cover and I figured that's entirely too many. And the only one that anybody had ever heard of was Charles Smith at that time nobody had ever heard of Ramsey either. But since he was working for the publisher and it was his idea and his book more or less, naturally his name should have gone on the cover and it did. So I didn't worry about my name not going on the cover. I wouldn't have wanted it on the cover anyway. but it would have been a little silly to have four people. And as I said, it turned out that Steve Smith didn't have time to do much work on the book after he opened his store. So the store did open then just about the time the book was ready to go to press a few months before the store opened actually. It went to press I think in July of 1939. So as far as the actual editing goes, Ramsey would have done most of that as far as proofreading and tended to the business of getting the photographs. Other people did a lot of work like Charles Smith was down here in New Orleans in the spring of 1939 and dug up quite a few of those photos. Especially the ones that are marked from Sidney Desveen. And the Bolden picture, Charles Smith dug that up from Carnish and got a new negative and everything made here. And I'd gotten quite a few pictures in Chicago. I took some myself. For instance, the Dodds picture and the Jimmy Yancey, maybe one or two others. And also dug up quite a few that Bill Johnson, the bass player, had. He had quite a collection of pictures and I borrowed those and took them to New York. But anyway, Ramsey's the one that put all that stuff together and organized the book after the material came in.
